paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of samples (%) across two measures of ambiguity: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity Std (Outer)," displays four segments corresponding to different standard deviation values: Std: 0.0 (dark blue, 49.0%), Std: 0.47 (medium dark blue, 38.0%), Std: 0.82 (medium blue, 7.0%), and Std: 0.94 (light blue, 5.0%). The inner ring, labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)," shows three segments for maximum ambiguity levels: Max: 1 (light blue, 39.0%), Max: 2 (very light blue, 47.7%), and Max: 3 (lightest blue, 14.2%). Both rings are segmented in descending order of percentage, with the largest proportions in each ring representing lower ambiguity levels. The chart indicates that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity, with nearly half of the samples having zero standard deviation and the largest single category in the inner ring being Max: 2.
